title: Unrolled sums with a saving macro
description:
Write two macros and three functions:

- `SAVE` and `RESTORE`: push and pop `rbx`, `r12` and `r13` (restore in reverse order).
- `sum8(array)`: the sum of exactly 8 qwords, unrolled with `%rep` and `%assign` (no loop).
- `dot4(a, b)`: the dot product of two arrays of exactly 4 qwords, also unrolled.
- `sum_blocks(array, count)`: the sum of `count` qwords (count is a multiple of 8), calling `sum8` for each block of 8. It keeps its own values in `rbx`, `r12` and `r13` across the calls, saved and restored with your macros.

The tests check that `rbx`, `rbp` and `r12` to `r15` survive every call.

starter.solution.asm:
%macro SAVE 0
%endmacro

%macro RESTORE 0
%endmacro

sum8:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

dot4:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

sum_blocks:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
%macro SAVE 0
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        push    r13
%endmacro

%macro RESTORE 0
        pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
%endmacro

sum8:
        xor     eax, eax
%assign i 0
%rep 8
        add     rax, [rdi + i * 8]
%assign i i + 1
%endrep
        ret

dot4:
        xor     eax, eax
%assign i 0
%rep 4
        mov     rcx, [rdi + i * 8]
        imul    rcx, [rsi + i * 8]
        add     rax, rcx
%assign i i + 1
%endrep
        ret

sum_blocks:
        SAVE
        mov     rbx, rdi                ; the next block
        lea     r12, [rdi + rsi*8]      ; the end
        xor     r13d, r13d              ; the total
.loop:  cmp     rbx, r12
        jae     .done
        mov     rdi, rbx
        call    sum8
        add     r13, rax
        add     rbx, 64
        jmp     .loop
.done:  mov     rax, r13
        RESTORE
        ret

hints: `%assign i 0` before `%rep`, and `%assign i i + 1` at the end of its body: each copy then uses the next offset, `[rdi + i * 8]`.

`sum_blocks` calls `sum8`, which may change any scratch register, so its own pointer, end and total must live in `rbx`, `r12` and `r13`, which is exactly why `SAVE` and `RESTORE` exist. Three pushes also leave `rsp` 16-byte aligned for the call.
